# Why Kanaloa is spelled that way — and what it costs to get it right

There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *kanaloa*. This is the file on how **Kanaloa** replaced it.

Hawaiian myths present Kānāloa as a complementary power to Kāne, the creator. Their partnership structures much of traditional cosmology.

## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Kanaloa
- **ASCII form:** kanaloa
- **Meaning:** "Hawaiian god symbolized by the squid or by the octopus, typically associated with Kāne"
- **Domain of influence:** Ocean, Underworld
- **Pantheon:** Polynesian
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 190 of 397

## The Name Before the Marks


Spoken, the name runs `/kaːˈnaːloa/` — 'kah-NAH-loh-ah' — both 'a' vowels are long, and the name flows like a slow wave.

## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Kanaloa** lives at [/sites/kanaloa/](/sites/kanaloa/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/kanaloa/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/kanaloa/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/kanaloa/patterns/).

One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

## The Archetype at Work

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) seats this temple in **3 industries**, each match argued and weighted: **Maritime, Shipping & Ocean Industries** (the Hawaiian god of the deep salt ocean, the octopus whose arms reach in all directions like the currents.); **Funerary & Memorial Services** (ocean and underworld; the deep as final home.); **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** (ocean and underworld together; Polynesian mythic depth.). The [Resonance File](/sites/kanaloa/blog/resonance/) reads those seats through the myths themselves.

## In the Sacred Texts

The Polynesian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Kumulipo](/texts/kumulipo/) and [Polynesian Mythology](/texts/polynesian-mythology/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

## The Emblems

The name does not travel alone. **Octopus (heʻe)** — The many-armed creature of the deep, Kānāloa's kin or avatar.; **Ocean waves** — The visible movement of his vast body.; **Kava plant** — A plant of ritual and healing associated with him.. Each emblem is filed in the temple's record with its own provenance, the same discipline the spelling gets.

## For the Voice

'kah-NAH-loh-ah' — both 'a' vowels are long, and the name flows like a slow wave. The reconstructed line runs `/kaːˈnaːloa/` — the temple's pronunciation atlas carries the phonemes one by one.

## The Discipline It Answers To

This restoration belongs to Polynesian, a tradition that navigated by names the way it navigated by stars. The rules that govern it are not house style; they are the tradition's own scholarship, applied with the same care here as in any edition — and published, with the sources, so the file can be checked the way an edition can be checked. One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.
